text: Databases store and organise information so we can find it quickly. In a relational database, data sits in tables with rows and columns, and we use SQL to write queries that retrieve or change it. NoSQL databases work differently, storing flexible documents or key-value pairs instead of strict tables. Data modelling helps you plan how data connects before you build anything. Indexes make searches much faster, like a book's index, though they use extra space. Choosing between SQL and NoSQL depends on your needs: structured data suits SQL, while fast-changing or unstructured data often fits NoSQL better.
